#        

## **1\. Purpose of the Activity** {#1.-purpose-of-the-activity}

The primary objective of this phase is to translate the initial concept of an **AI-driven Legal Support Assistant for Event Organizers** into an actionable, unambiguous, and verifiable Software Requirements Specification (SRS).

At this stage, the focus is strictly on **problem domain definition**, not solution implementation. The project transitions from high-level intentions into explicit capabilities, operational constraints, and boundaries before any architectural or code-level decisions take place.

Initial Concept ─ Stakeholder Needs ── Requirements Specification ──System Design and Build

The scope of this activity establishes:

**Who** interacts with the platform (event producers, venue managers, legal/compliance reviewers).

**What** specific operational workflows the software must execute (contract verification, permit discovery, risk profiling).

**Under what constraints** the system must function (admissibility, jurisdiction limits, non-liability disclaimers, multi-tenant isolation).

**How** the delivered software will be objectively measured and accepted during validation and verification testing.

## **2\. Why Requirements Specification is Important for this System** {#2.-why-requirements-specification-is-important-for-this-system}

In high-stakes, liability-heavy environments like legal compliance for live entertainment, vague requirements introduce operational and legal risks:

Ambiguous definition: *"The system should use AI to help event organizers review their contracts."*

*Unresolved risks:* What jurisdictions are supported? Does "review" imply automated redaction, clause risk scoring, or legal liability? What happens if an event producer executes a contract missing a force majeure clause based on a missing retrieval chunk?

Clear specification: *"The system shall evaluate uploaded vendor contracts against municipal noise and safety regulations, flag missing indemnification clauses, assign an objective compliance status (Compliant, Conditional, Critical Risk), and present the extracted clause alongside the relevant statutory citation for mandatory user sign-off."*

By decoupling requirements from premature design:

**Requirement:** The system shall restrict contract clause retrieval strictly to the legal jurisdiction designated for that specific event.

**Premature Design (Avoid at this stage):** POST /api/v1/vectors/search?filter={"jurisdiction": "CDMX"} using Qdrant and HNSW indexing.

## **4\. Current Process** {#4.-current-process}

Event organizers typically coordinate legal compliance across fragmented, manual, and unstandardized communication channels.

### **Process Characteristics** {#process-characteristics}

| Dimension | Real-World As-Is State |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Trigger** | Securing an event date or receiving a vendor agreement (artist rider, venue lease, audio rental). |
| **Actors** | Event Producer, Production Coordinator, External Legal Counsel (intermittent), Municipal Licensing Clerk. |
| **Information Inputs** | Unstructured PDFs, email threads, WhatsApp messages, scanned paper forms, outdated municipal gazettes. |
| **Manual Activities** | Manual cross-referencing of venue contracts against artist riders; manual lookup of municipal noise ordinances and civil protection regulations. |
| **Bottlenecks and Delays** | External legal counsel turnaround takes 5–10 business days per contract; producers bypass formal review due to ticketing deadlines. |
| **Error Modes** | Overlooking indemnification limits, omitting severe-weather force majeure clauses, assuming a venue's permit covers alcohol distribution. |
| **Records Produced** | Dispersed PDF contracts stored on personal cloud drives; lack of unified audit trails for compliance validation. |

### **As-Is Flow** {#as-is-flow}

Contract/Rider Arrives  
       
Producer Manual Review ── (Incomplete / Non-specialized check)  
         Send to External Lawyer ── Wait 5-10 Days ── High Cost / Project Delayed  
             Bypass Review due to Urgency                          
             Manual Feedback Applied  
             High Liability Exposure ─  (Noise fines, non-covered cancellations,  
             licensing shutdowns)

## **5\. Desired Process: To-Be Process Model** {#5.-desired-process:-to-be-process-model}

The To-Be workflow introduces structured intake, automated schema verification, retrieval-augmented legal analysis, and an explicit human-in-the-loop decision checkpoint.

### **Classification of Workflows** {#classification-of-workflows}

![][image2]

| Automation (Rule-based / OS) | AI Support (RAG / Gemma-Gemini) | Human Decision (Accountable Operator) |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Document parsing | Semantic chunk retrieval | Assessing acceptable operational risk |
| Metadata tagging | Missing clause scoring | Final contract execution |
| Format validation | Risk summarization | Submitting permit files |
| Audit trail logs | Regulatory cross-check |  |

### **To-Be Process Sequence** {#to-be-process-sequence}

Producer Inputs Event Details and Uploads Contract  
                   (Automation)

System extracts text, validates format, tags metadata: Jurisdiction, Venue Type, Aforo  
                   (AI Support: Gemma Vectorization \+ RAG Retrieval)

System matches contract clauses against local statutes, sound regulations and safety standards  
                  (AI Support: Gemini Analysis)

System flags conflicting clauses, highlights liabilities, and generates audit checklist  
                  (Automation)

System outputs structured risk profile with explicit statutory citations and disclaimers  
                   (Human Decision)

Producer / Legal Officer reviews highlighted clauses, accepts/modifies, approves final version  
                   (Automation)

Final contract version and compliance audit log archived to project registry

### **Process Traceability Matrix** {#process-traceability-matrix}

| Process Step | Action Type | System Capability Requirement | Verification Method |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **1\. Ingestion** | Automation | The system shall parse legal agreements in PDF/DOCX formats and extract key metadata within 10 seconds. | Automated file parser benchmark test. |
| **2\. Contextualization** | AI Support | The system shall identify the active legal jurisdiction and retrieve applicable statutory requirements. | Precision/Recall analysis on test set of municipal event regulations. |
| **3\. Risk Scoring** | AI Support | The system shall cross-reference supplier agreements against standard risk policies (cancellation, force majeure, indemnity). | Blind test comparing AI risk flags against a lawyer-annotated gold standard. |
| **4\. Validation** | Human Decision | The system shall require the producer to acknowledge each flagged risk before marking a document as ready for execution. | User workflow state transition verification. |
| **5\. Traceability** | Automation | The system shall generate an immutable timestamped log of all retrieved citations, model outputs, and user approvals. | Database inspection and audit export validation. |

## **6\. Identify Functional Requirements** {#6.-identify-functional-requirements}

Functional requirements define what the AI-driven Legal Support Assistant for Event Organizers must do. The requirements below were derived from the stakeholder needs, the As-Is and To-Be processes already documented in this specification, the project objectives, the audited business rules, and the human-in-the-loop legal safeguards established in the previous planning activity.  
Requirement syntax: FR-XXX: The system shall allow \[actor\] to \[action\] \[object\] \[condition, if applicable\]. Requirements are written as independent, verifiable statements so that each one can later be linked to a use case and a test case.

### **Requirements Table** {#requirements-table}

| ID | Functional requirement | Actor | Priority | Source |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-001 | The system shall allow a new user to create an account by providing a name, email address, password, and acceptance of the privacy notice and legal disclaimer. | Event Producer / Reviewer | Must | Stakeholder need; access control |
| FR-002 | The system shall allow a registered user to sign in, sign out, recover account access, and terminate active sessions. | Registered User | Must | Stakeholder need; security |
| FR-003 | The system shall restrict administrative functions to authorized Administrator accounts and shall prevent standard users from accessing another user's private cases, documents, or consultation history. | System / Administrator | Must | Security rule; audited NFR |
| FR-004 | The system shall allow an Event Producer to create an event case containing event name, date, venue, city/state, jurisdiction, venue type, expected capacity, and responsible organization. | Event Producer | Must | To-Be intake; project objective |
| FR-005 | The system shall allow an authorized user to upload, list, open, associate, and delete legal documents in supported PDF, DOCX, and TXT formats within an event case. | Event Producer / Reviewer | Must | To-Be ingestion; stakeholder need |
| FR-006 | When a supported PDF does not contain usable text, the system shall offer text extraction from the scanned document before legal analysis or indexing. | System | Should | Document ingestion; accessibility of evidence |
| FR-007 | When a legal document is uploaded, the system shall extract available metadata including document type, parties, dates, jurisdiction, venue, and event reference. | System | Must | To-Be contextualization |
| FR-008 | The system shall classify an uploaded document into a supported legal-document category such as venue agreement, artist agreement, supplier agreement, sponsorship agreement, waiver, permit, policy, or regulation. | System | Should | Document workflow; AI support |
| FR-009 | The system shall allow an authorized user to submit a legal-support question in natural language and receive a structured preliminary response associated with the selected event case. | Event Producer / Reviewer | Must | Stakeholder need; project purpose |
| FR-010 | Before generating a jurisdiction-specific legal response, the system shall use the event jurisdiction and relevant date and shall request missing context when that information is insufficient. | System / User | Must | BR jurisdiction rule |
| FR-011 | The system shall identify and label relevant clauses in uploaded contracts, including cancellation, indemnification, force majeure, liability, payment, termination, insurance, and data-protection clauses when present. | System | Must | Contract review workflow |
| FR-012 | The system shall extract parties, obligations, deadlines, payment conditions, penalties, renewal terms, and other material conditions when they are explicitly present in the analyzed document. | System | Must | Contract review workflow |
| FR-013 | The system shall flag potential missing clauses, internal inconsistencies, conflicting obligations, unsupported assumptions, and other areas that may require professional legal review. | System | Must | Risk profiling objective |
| FR-014 | The system shall compare supported contract provisions and event information against applicable approved legal sources retrieved for the selected jurisdiction and date. | System | Must | To-Be regulatory cross-check |
| FR-015 | The system shall generate a preliminary compliance checklist for an event, including potentially applicable civil protection, capacity, noise, copyright/music, alcohol, accessibility, and other permit or licensing requirements supported by the knowledge base. | Event Producer / System | Must | Permit discovery workflow |
| FR-016 | The system shall provide source-backed preliminary information about cancellation, postponement, refunds, penalties, severe weather, health emergencies, artist cancellation, and force-majeure considerations when relevant sources are available. | Event Producer / Reviewer | Must | Contingency stakeholder need |
| FR-017 | The system shall provide source-backed preliminary information about civil liability, insurance requirements, equipment coverage, waivers, and allocation of responsibility when supported by available sources. | Event Producer / Reviewer | Should | Liability stakeholder need |
| FR-018 | The system shall identify privacy and consent considerations related to attendee data, accreditations, contact lists, photographs, video, recordings, and other personal-data processing associated with the event. | Event Producer / Reviewer | Must | Privacy stakeholder need |
| FR-019 | The system shall allow an authorized user to generate and edit preliminary event-related contract clauses or templates while preserving the mandatory legal-review disclaimer. | Event Producer / Reviewer | Must | Drafting objective; BR human review |
| FR-020 | For each source-backed legal statement, the system shall display the source title and, when available, the article or section, jurisdiction, authority level, effective date, and version. | System | Must | Traceability rule; RAG safeguard |
| FR-021 | The system shall require the responsible user to acknowledge each Critical Risk finding before a reviewed document can be marked Ready for Execution. | Event Producer / Legal Reviewer | Must | Human decision checkpoint |
| FR-022 | The system shall allow users to save consultations, reopen previous conversations, and associate consultation history with the corresponding event case. | Registered User | Should | Case continuity need |
| FR-023 | The system shall allow an authorized user to export a readable legal-support summary containing the question or document reviewed, detected risks, cited sources, disclaimer, and user acknowledgements. | Event Producer / Reviewer | Should | Auditability; records need |
| FR-024 | The system shall allow an Administrator to add, update, deactivate, remove, and re-index approved legal sources while preserving source and version metadata. | Administrator | Must | Knowledge-base governance |
| FR-025 | The system shall allow a user to report an answer, citation, or risk flag as inaccurate, outdated, unclear, or incomplete for later review without automatically altering the approved source base. | Registered User | Should | Feedback / QA need |
| FR-026 | The system shall allow a user to request export or deletion of stored personal data and account-associated content according to the defined retention policy. | Registered User | Must | Privacy and data lifecycle rule |

   
The catalogue contains more than 20 functional requirements because the project includes separate, independently testable capabilities for document intake, legal analysis, event compliance, human review, traceability, administration, and privacy controls.

 

## **7\. Use Cases** {#7.-use-cases}

Each major system capability is represented through a use case. The model below links the main actors to the workflows that support the legal-assistance process.

### **Use Case Model** {#use-case-model}

| Actor | Associated use cases |
| :---- | :---- |
| Event Producer | UC-001 Register and Authenticate; UC-002 Create Event Case; UC-003 Upload and Analyze Contract; UC-004 Ask a Legal-Support Question; UC-005 Generate Preliminary Clause or Template; UC-006 Generate Compliance Checklist; UC-007 Review and Acknowledge Risks; UC-009 Export Legal-Support Record. |
| Legal / Compliance Reviewer | UC-003 Upload and Analyze Contract; UC-004 Ask a Legal-Support Question; UC-005 Generate Preliminary Clause or Template; UC-006 Generate Compliance Checklist; UC-007 Review and Acknowledge Risks; UC-009 Export Legal-Support Record. |
| Administrator | UC-001 Register and Authenticate; UC-008 Manage Approved Legal Sources; review user feedback and audit logs. |
| AI / RAG Services | Support retrieval, source-backed generation, risk extraction, citation, and insufficient-evidence behavior in UC-003, UC-004, UC-005, and UC-006. |

 

### **UC-001 — Register and Authenticate** {#uc-001-—-register-and-authenticate}

**Primary actor:** Event Producer, Legal/Compliance Reviewer, or Administrator  
**Supporting actors:** Authentication service  
**Goal:** Create or access an authorized account while enforcing role and credential controls.  
**Preconditions:** The web application is available. For sign-in, the account already exists and is active.  
**Trigger:** The user selects Register, Sign In, Password Recovery, or Sign Out.  
Main flow:  
1\. The user selects the required authentication action.  
2\. The system displays the corresponding form.  
3\. The user provides the required credentials or registration information.  
4\. The system validates the submitted data and account status.  
5\. For an Administrator account, the system requires the configured second authentication factor.  
6\. The system creates or restores the authenticated session and applies the user role.  
7\. The system records the authentication event and displays the authorized workspace.  
**Alternative flows:** If registration data are incomplete or the email is already registered, the system identifies the problem and requests correction.  
**Exception flows:** If credentials are invalid or repeated failed attempts exceed the security threshold, access is denied and the protective mechanism is applied.  
**Postconditions:** A valid authenticated session exists, or the access attempt is safely rejected and logged.  
**Related requirements:** FR-001, FR-002, FR-003; NFR-005, NFR-006, NFR-009.  
 

### **UC-002 — Create Event Case** {#uc-002-—-create-event-case}

**Primary actor:** Event Producer  
**Supporting actors:** Legal/Compliance Reviewer (optional)  
**Goal:** Create a structured case that supplies the jurisdiction and event context needed for later legal-support activities.  
**Preconditions:** The user is authenticated and has permission to create a case.  
**Trigger:** The user selects New Event Case.  
Main flow:  
1\. The system displays the event intake form.  
2\. The user enters event name, date, venue, location/jurisdiction, venue type, capacity, and organization information.  
3\. The system validates required fields.  
4\. The system creates the event case and assigns a unique case identifier.  
5\. The system displays the case dashboard and makes it available for document and consultation association.  
**Alternative flows:** The user may save a draft when non-critical information is still unavailable.  
**Exception flows:** If jurisdiction or event date is missing, the system allows the draft to be saved but marks jurisdiction-specific analysis as unavailable until the required context is completed.  
**Postconditions:** A persistent event case exists with the supplied context and an auditable creation timestamp.  
**Related requirements:** FR-004, FR-010, FR-022; BR-003.  
 

### **UC-003 — Upload and Analyze Contract** {#uc-003-—-upload-and-analyze-contract}

**Primary actor:** Event Producer or Legal/Compliance Reviewer  
**Supporting actors:** Document parser, OCR service, RAG retrieval service, LLM service  
**Goal:** Review an uploaded event-related agreement, extract key conditions, flag risks, and show supporting legal evidence.  
**Preconditions:** The user is authenticated; an event case exists; the file is a supported type.  
**Trigger:** The user selects Upload Document or Analyze Contract within an event case.  
Main flow:  
1\. The user selects a PDF, DOCX, or TXT legal document.  
2\. The system validates file type, size, and security controls.  
3\. The system extracts text and, if needed, offers OCR for a scanned PDF.  
4\. The system extracts document metadata and classifies the document type.  
5\. The system identifies relevant clauses and extracts obligations, dates, penalties, and other material conditions.  
6\. The system retrieves approved legal sources for the event jurisdiction and relevant date.  
7\. The system flags supported missing clauses, inconsistencies, and risk areas.  
8\. The system displays the findings with source citations, confidence/limitation information, and the mandatory disclaimer.  
9\. The system stores the review results and audit information in the event case.  
**Alternative flows:** The user may review the extracted text and correct document metadata before legal analysis.  
**Exception flows:** If the document is unreadable, malicious, unsupported, or lacks sufficient legal evidence, the system stops or limits analysis and explains the reason rather than generating unsupported legal conclusions.  
**Postconditions:** The document, extracted information, findings, citations, and audit metadata are stored or the analysis is safely rejected with a recorded reason.  
**Related requirements:** FR-005 through FR-014, FR-020; AIR-001 through AIR-010.  
 

### **UC-004 — Ask a Legal-Support Question** {#uc-004-—-ask-a-legal-support-question}

**Primary actor:** Event Producer or Legal/Compliance Reviewer  
**Supporting actors:** RAG retrieval service and LLM service  
**Goal:** Obtain a preliminary, source-backed answer about an event-related legal or compliance issue.  
**Preconditions:** The user is authenticated and an event case or sufficient jurisdiction/date context is available.  
**Trigger:** The user enters a legal-support question in the consultation interface.  
Main flow:  
1\. The user submits a question.  
2\. The system reads the event context and requests missing jurisdiction/date information when required.  
3\. The system searches only approved sources applicable to the supported scope and context.  
4\. The system generates a structured answer grounded in retrieved evidence.  
5\. The system displays source citations, conflicting-source notices when applicable, uncertainty/abstention when evidence is insufficient, and the mandatory disclaimer.  
6\. The user may save the consultation to the event case.  
**Alternative flows:** The user may refine the question or provide additional facts when the system requests clarification.  
**Exception flows:** If the question is outside the supported event-law scope or evidence is insufficient, the system states the limitation and does not invent legal authority.  
**Postconditions:** A traceable consultation is displayed and optionally stored with its sources and context.  
**Related requirements:** FR-009, FR-010, FR-020, FR-022; BR-001 through BR-006; AIR-001 through AIR-009.  
 

### **UC-005 — Generate Preliminary Clause or Template** {#uc-005-—-generate-preliminary-clause-or-template}

**Primary actor:** Event Producer or Legal/Compliance Reviewer  
**Supporting actors:** RAG retrieval service and LLM service  
**Goal:** Create an editable preliminary event-related clause or template that is clearly marked for professional review.  
**Preconditions:** The user is authenticated; event context is available; the requested document type is within project scope.  
**Trigger:** The user selects Generate Clause/Template and specifies the requested content.  
Main flow:  
1\. The system asks for the agreement type and relevant event context.  
2\. The user provides required details.  
3\. The system retrieves applicable approved source material when available.  
4\. The system generates an editable preliminary clause or template.  
5\. The system identifies assumptions or missing information and displays supporting citations for legal claims.  
6\. The system displays the mandatory legal-review disclaimer before the text can be exported.  
7\. The user edits or saves the draft to the event case.  
**Alternative flows:** The user may request a revised draft after changing facts or selecting another supported clause type.  
**Exception flows:** If the system lacks reliable supporting evidence for a jurisdiction-specific provision, it must omit the unsupported legal assertion or clearly mark it as requiring professional review.  
**Postconditions:** An editable preliminary draft is stored with its generation context, sources, and disclaimer.  
**Related requirements:** FR-019, FR-020, FR-023; BR-002, BR-007; AIR-001, AIR-002, AIR-003.  
 

### **UC-006 — Generate Event Compliance Checklist** {#uc-006-—-generate-event-compliance-checklist}

**Primary actor:** Event Producer  
**Supporting actors:** Legal/Compliance Reviewer, RAG retrieval service  
**Goal:** Identify potentially applicable event permits, licensing, safety, capacity, noise, copyright/music, alcohol, privacy, and related compliance topics.  
**Preconditions:** The user is authenticated and the event case contains jurisdiction, venue, date, and basic event characteristics.  
**Trigger:** The user selects Compliance Checklist.  
Main flow:  
1\. The system reads event context.  
2\. The system retrieves applicable approved regulatory sources.  
3\. The system evaluates the supported compliance categories against the event information.  
4\. The system generates a checklist showing requirement, status, evidence/source, responsible party, and unresolved information.  
5\. The system marks items that require external authority confirmation or professional review.  
6\. The user saves the checklist and may assign follow-up actions outside the AI decision itself.  
**Alternative flows:** If some event details are missing, the system generates only the supported subset and lists the missing data needed for a more complete checklist.  
**Exception flows:** If no approved sources cover the selected jurisdiction or date, the system states that the checklist cannot be treated as complete and does not fabricate permit requirements.  
**Postconditions:** A source-backed preliminary checklist is stored in the event case.  
**Related requirements:** FR-015 through FR-018, FR-020; BR-003 through BR-006; AIR-004 through AIR-008.  
 

### **UC-007 — Review and Acknowledge Risks** {#uc-007-—-review-and-acknowledge-risks}

**Primary actor:** Event Producer or Legal/Compliance Reviewer  
**Supporting actors:** System audit-log service  
**Goal:** Ensure a human decision-maker reviews flagged risks before a document is treated as ready for execution.  
**Preconditions:** A document analysis has produced one or more risk findings.  
**Trigger:** The user opens the Risk Review panel or attempts to mark the document Ready for Execution.  
Main flow:  
1\. The system lists each risk finding with severity, supporting document excerpt, legal source citation, and limitation note.  
2\. The user reviews each finding.  
3\. The user may add a comment, mark it addressed, or request additional review.  
4\. For each Critical Risk, the user explicitly acknowledges the finding.  
5\. The system prevents the Ready for Execution state until all required acknowledgements are complete.  
6\. The system records the user, timestamp, and acknowledgement action.  
**Alternative flows:** A Legal/Compliance Reviewer may return the document to the Event Producer with comments instead of approving the readiness state.  
**Exception flows:** If a cited source becomes inactive or unavailable, the system marks the affected finding for re-review before final readiness.  
**Postconditions:** The document is either held for further action or marked Ready for Execution with a traceable human acknowledgement record.  
**Related requirements:** FR-013, FR-020, FR-021, FR-023; BR-007; NFR-010.  
 

### **UC-008 — Manage Approved Legal Sources** {#uc-008-—-manage-approved-legal-sources}

**Primary actor:** Administrator  
**Supporting actors:** Document ingestion, embedding/vectorization, audit-log services  
**Goal:** Maintain the curated legal knowledge base used by retrieval without losing source/version traceability.  
**Preconditions:** The Administrator is authenticated with MFA and has source-management permission.  
**Trigger:** The Administrator selects Legal Source Management.  
Main flow:  
1\. The Administrator adds, updates, deactivates, or removes an approved source.  
2\. The system validates required metadata such as jurisdiction, authority level, effective date, status, and version.  
3\. The system stores the source and creates or updates its searchable representation.  
4\. The system deactivates superseded material when appropriate without silently deleting audit history.  
5\. The system records the administrative action, source version, user, and timestamp.  
**Alternative flows:** The Administrator may preview extraction and metadata before publishing the source to active retrieval.  
**Exception flows:** If required metadata are missing or indexing fails, the system keeps the source inactive and reports the failure.  
**Postconditions:** The active knowledge base reflects the approved change and retains auditable version metadata.  
**Related requirements:** FR-024; BR-004 through BR-006; NFR-005 through NFR-011; AIR-004, AIR-005, AIR-009.

## **8\. Identify Non-Functional Requirements** {#8.-identify-non-functional-requirements}

Non-functional requirements describe how well the system must operate and the constraints that protect legal data, users, and the reliability of AI-assisted outputs. The statements below are measurable wherever practical and avoid vague terms such as “fast,” “secure,” or “user-friendly.”

| ID | Category | Non-functional requirement | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NFR-001 | Performance | Under the defined acceptance test load, at least 95% of non-AI interface requests shall complete within 3 seconds, excluding file-upload transfer time. | Must |
| NFR-002 | AI response time | For ordinary consultations that do not require OCR, at least 90% of AI requests shall begin returning a response within 15 seconds under the defined acceptance test load. | Should |
| NFR-003 | Availability | The production service shall target at least 99% monthly availability, excluding announced maintenance windows. | Should |
| NFR-004 | Transport security | All production web traffic shall use HTTPS with a currently supported TLS configuration. | Must |
| NFR-005 | Credential security | Passwords shall be stored using a modern adaptive password-hashing algorithm, and Administrator accounts shall use multi-factor authentication. | Must |
| NFR-006 | Encryption at rest | Confidential documents, consultation data, and protected authentication secrets stored by the platform shall be encrypted at rest or protected by an equivalent managed-storage control. | Must |
| NFR-007 | Authorization and isolation | A user shall not be able to read, modify, retrieve, or search another user's private cases, documents, or consultation history without explicit authorization. | Must |
| NFR-008 | File security | Uploaded files shall be validated by supported type and size and shall be scanned, sandboxed, or isolated against malicious content before entering the AI processing pipeline. | Must |
| NFR-009 | Abuse protection | Authentication endpoints and high-cost AI endpoints shall apply rate limiting, and repeated failed sign-in attempts shall trigger a temporary protective control. | Must |
| NFR-010 | Auditability | The platform shall record authentication failures, administrative source changes, legal-source versions, document analysis events, model/prompt versions, retrieval source identifiers, risk acknowledgements, and exports with timestamps. | Must |
| NFR-011 | Privacy and retention | The platform shall define retention/deletion periods for user documents and consultations and shall not use private user content to train models without separate explicit consent. | Must |
| NFR-012 | Accessibility | The main authentication, consultation, upload, document-review, history, and export flows shall be tested against applicable WCAG 2.1 Level AA criteria for keyboard access, labels, focus, contrast, and understandable error messages. | Should |
| NFR-013 | Browser compatibility | The web application shall support the two most recent stable versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari at the time of release. | Should |
| NFR-014 | Responsive design | The main user workflows shall be usable on desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts without horizontal scrolling in the primary content area. | Should |
| NFR-015 | Backup and recovery | Application data and legal-source metadata shall be backed up on a documented schedule, and at least one successful restoration test shall be documented before production release. | Must |
| NFR-016 | Maintainability and testing | Critical authentication, authorization, deletion, retrieval, citation, and risk-acknowledgement functions shall have automated tests, and environment-specific configuration shall be separated from source code. | Should |
| NFR-017 | Secrets management | API keys, model credentials, database passwords, signing secrets, and similar credentials shall not be stored directly in source code or committed to version control. | Must |

 

 

## **9\. Define Business Rules and Constraints** {#9.-define-business-rules-and-constraints}

Business rules express legal-domain and organizational policies that constrain system behavior. Constraints describe solution restrictions, assumptions state conditions believed to be true, and dependencies identify external elements required for operation.

### **Business Rules** {#business-rules}

| ID | Rule | Business rule |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| BR-001 | Defined legal scope | The first release is limited to preliminary legal support for event organization and related contracts, permits, compliance, liability, and privacy topics. Questions outside this supported domain shall be identified as outside scope. |
| BR-002 | No replacement of professional counsel | The application shall not present itself as a law firm or substitute for a licensed lawyer. Binding or high-impact decisions shall be marked for professional review. |
| BR-003 | Jurisdiction visibility | The jurisdiction and relevant date used for a jurisdiction-specific answer shall be visible. If the context is missing or insufficient, the system shall request it or explicitly state the limitation. |
| BR-004 | No invented legal authority | The system shall not fabricate statutes, articles, cases, agencies, permits, or citations. If evidence is insufficient, the response shall state that the claim cannot be reliably supported by the available sources. |
| BR-005 | Source validity and hierarchy | Approved legal sources shall store jurisdiction, effective date, status/version, source type, and authority level when available so active primary authority can be distinguished from superseded or secondary material. |
| BR-006 | Conflicting sources | When relevant sources materially conflict, the system shall disclose the conflict and present the competing sources instead of silently selecting one as unquestionably correct. |
| BR-007 | Human review before binding use | Generated contracts, clauses, summaries, risk profiles, and compliance suggestions shall remain preliminary and editable and shall require human review before signature, filing, payment, cancellation, or another binding action. |
| BR-008 | Deletion consistency | When a user document is deleted, the system shall remove or deactivate associated extracted text, chunks, embeddings, and retrieval references according to the retention policy. |
| BR-009 | Private-content training restriction | Private uploaded documents and consultations shall not be added to a training dataset without separate, explicit user consent. |
| BR-010 | Risk status vocabulary | Contract/compliance findings shall use the project status vocabulary Compliant, Conditional, or Critical Risk, with a short explanation and evidence for the assigned status. |

 

### **Constraints** {#constraints}

| ID | Constraint |
| :---- | :---- |
| CON-001 | The solution shall be delivered as a web application for the current project release. |
| CON-002 | The system shall operate within the academic project schedule and available development resources; features outside the approved first-release scope shall be treated as future work or require formal scope approval. |
| CON-003 | The legal-assistance component shall use retrieval-augmented generation or an equivalent grounding mechanism based on a curated legal knowledge base; it shall not rely on unconstrained model memory for jurisdiction-specific legal claims. |
| CON-004 | Only supported document formats and maximum file sizes defined by the implementation configuration shall be accepted for analysis. |
| CON-005 | Any external AI, OCR, storage, or authentication service used by the implementation shall comply with the project privacy and security requirements. |
| CON-006 | The first release shall not autonomously sign contracts, submit government filings, make payments, cancel events, or make legally binding decisions on behalf of the user. |

 

### **Assumptions** {#assumptions}

| ID | Assumption |
| :---- | :---- |
| ASM-001 | Authorized users have reliable internet access and a supported modern web browser. |
| ASM-002 | Users provide truthful and sufficiently complete event facts, especially jurisdiction, event date, venue, and relevant contract documents. |
| ASM-003 | The project team can obtain and maintain a curated set of approved legal and regulatory sources for the jurisdictions included in the pilot. |
| ASM-004 | Uploaded documents are legally available to the user for review and processing within the application. |
| ASM-005 | A responsible human user remains accountable for final legal and operational decisions. |

 

### **Dependencies** {#dependencies}

| ID | Dependency |
| :---- | :---- |
| DEP-001 | Authentication and authorization service or library. |
| DEP-002 | Relational database and secure file/object storage. |
| DEP-003 | Embedding model and vector retrieval component for the curated knowledge base. |
| DEP-004 | LLM service or locally hosted approved model for structured response generation. |
| DEP-005 | OCR capability for scanned documents when OCR support is enabled. |
| DEP-006 | Curated legal/regulatory source collection with jurisdiction, date, status, and authority metadata. |
| DEP-007 | Hosting, logging, backup, and monitoring infrastructure. |

 

 

## **10\. Specify the AI Requirements** {#10.-specify-the-ai-requirements}

The AI component is specified as a set of explicit capabilities and safeguards rather than the vague statement “the system will use AI.” The following requirements define purpose, inputs, processing, outputs, human control, data sources, quality evaluation, and failure behavior.

| ID | AI capability | AI requirement | Priority |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| AIR-001 | Grounded legal-support generation | When a supported legal question or document review is processed, the AI shall base legally relevant claims on approved retrieved sources when such sources exist. | Must |
| AIR-002 | Evidence display | The AI output shall display the passages, references, or source identifiers supporting the main legal statements so the user can verify them. | Must |
| AIR-003 | Insufficient-evidence behavior | When retrieval produces weak, irrelevant, or insufficient evidence, the AI shall request additional context or state that it cannot support a reliable answer from the current knowledge base; it shall not invent legal authority. | Must |
| AIR-004 | Jurisdiction and temporal retrieval | The retrieval process shall filter or rank evidence according to the event jurisdiction, relevant date, source status, and supported matter context before generation. | Must |
| AIR-005 | Source freshness | The AI/RAG process shall prefer active/current sources and shall not present a superseded version as current when a newer active version is available in the knowledge base. | Must |
| AIR-006 | Authority hierarchy | Where source metadata are available, the system should prioritize primary or higher-authority legal sources over secondary explanatory material for jurisdiction-specific legal claims. | Should |
| AIR-007 | Conflict disclosure | When relevant retrieved sources materially disagree, the generated answer shall identify the disagreement and cite the competing sources. | Must |
| AIR-008 | Prompt-injection resistance | Uploaded documents and retrieved text shall be treated as untrusted data rather than system instructions. Embedded instructions that attempt to alter system behavior, reveal protected data, or bypass safeguards shall be isolated or ignored. | Must |
| AIR-009 | Sensitive-data minimization | The AI pipeline shall minimize transmission of personal or confidential information to external model services and shall follow configured privacy controls for any external processing. | Must |
| AIR-010 | Reproducibility and traceability | For auditable AI outputs, the system shall store the model/version, prompt/template version, retrieval parameters, source identifiers, event context, and timestamp required to investigate the result. | Must |
| AIR-011 | Risk classification | For supported contract/compliance analysis, the AI shall assign Compliant, Conditional, or Critical Risk only when the classification is accompanied by a short rationale and supporting document/source evidence. | Must |
| AIR-012 | Human control | AI output shall be treated as a recommendation, classification, extraction, or generated draft; it shall not automatically execute a legal or binding business action. | Must |
| AIR-013 | Retrieval-quality evaluation | Before release, the RAG pipeline shall be evaluated on a documented representative test set containing event-law questions and documents, including checks for source relevance, citation correctness, conflict handling, and insufficient-evidence behavior. | Must |
| AIR-014 | Feedback isolation | User feedback about an AI answer shall be stored for review but shall not automatically modify legal-source content or model behavior in production. | Should |

 

### **AI Requirement Definition** {#ai-requirement-definition}

| Dimension | Specification |
| :---- | :---- |
| Purpose | Reduce manual search time and support preliminary contract/compliance review without replacing professional legal judgment. |
| Input | User questions, event context, supported legal documents, and curated legal/regulatory source content. |
| Processing | Document parsing, metadata extraction, retrieval, evidence ranking, clause/obligation extraction, risk classification, grounded response generation, and citation assembly. |
| Output | Structured answers, contract findings, risk profiles, preliminary clauses/templates, compliance checklists, source citations, limitation notices, and audit metadata. |
| User | Event Producers, Legal/Compliance Reviewers, and Administrators for governance tasks. |
| Human control | Outputs are recommendations, classifications, extractions, or drafts. Human review is required before any binding use. |
| Data | Curated approved legal sources plus user-provided case documents and context; private content is governed by retention and training restrictions. |
| Quality | Evaluated through representative retrieval/citation tests, lawyer-annotated or expert-reviewed samples where available, and negative tests for unsupported or conflicting evidence. |
| Risk response | When evidence is insufficient, conflicting, outdated, or outside supported scope, the AI must disclose the limitation, abstain where necessary, and avoid fabricated authority. |

 

 

## **11\. Prioritize Requirements** {#11.-prioritize-requirements}

MoSCoW prioritization is used to control scope. Must items are required for a safe, useful first release; Should items materially improve quality but can be deferred if time is constrained; Could items are desirable enhancements; Won't items are explicitly excluded from the current release.

| Priority | Requirement groups / features | Justification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Must | Authentication, authorization, event-case context, document upload, legal question handling, contract analysis, jurisdiction control, citations, human risk acknowledgement, legal disclaimer, privacy/deletion, source administration, core security controls, grounded AI behavior, abstention, conflict disclosure, and AI traceability. | These capabilities are required to fulfill the project purpose while controlling legal, security, and AI reliability risks. |
| Should | OCR for scanned documents, document classification, liability guidance, saved consultation history, exportable summaries, user feedback, performance targets for AI response time, accessibility, browser compatibility, responsive layouts, maintainability tests, and source-authority prioritization. | Important for usability, operational continuity, and quality, but the system can still demonstrate its core legal-support workflow if some are staged after the first prototype. |
| Could | Advanced dashboards, collaborative comments, reminder notifications for permit deadlines, comparison between multiple contract versions, multilingual interface, and analytics on recurring risk categories. | Useful enhancements that do not determine whether the core legal-support workflow functions. |
| Won't | Native mobile application, autonomous contract signature, autonomous government filing, payment execution, event cancellation, court representation, and unrestricted legal advice outside the curated event-organization scope. | Excluded to avoid scope creep and because they would introduce responsibilities and integrations beyond the approved project. |

 

### **Priority Decisions for Core Requirements** {#priority-decisions-for-core-requirements}

| Requirement | Priority | Justification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| FR-003 / NFR-007 | Must | Required to prevent unauthorized access to private legal documents and case data. |
| FR-010 / BR-003 | Must | Jurisdiction and date determine which law may apply; answers cannot be treated as jurisdiction-specific without this context. |
| FR-020 / AIR-002 | Must | Citations are necessary for verification and traceability of legal-support outputs. |
| FR-021 / BR-007 | Must | Human acknowledgement prevents AI risk flags from becoming automatic binding decisions. |
| AIR-003 / BR-004 | Must | Abstention and no-invented-authority behavior directly reduce hallucinated legal guidance risk. |
| FR-006 | Should | OCR increases document coverage but can be postponed if the first prototype supports text-based PDFs and DOCX files. |
| FR-025 | Should | Feedback supports quality improvement, but it is not required to prove the primary contract-analysis workflow. |
| Advanced dashboard | Could | It improves presentation but does not add a core legal-assistance capability. |
| Native mobile application | Won't | The approved first release is a responsive web application. |

 

 

## **12\. Detect Ambiguity, Conflict and Missing Requirements** {#12.-detect-ambiguity,-conflict-and-missing-requirements}

The requirements were reviewed against the manual baseline audit and the later AI-assisted QA work. The matrix below records the main quality defects detected in earlier wording and the correction now incorporated into this SRS. The final requirement statements above are the corrected versions.

| Requirement / area | Problem detected | Type | Proposed correction |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Original general “legal AI” scope | Unclear whether the assistant covered all areas of law, which could cause uncontrolled expectations and design decisions. | Ambiguous / Scope violation | BR-001 limits release 1 to event-organization legal support and requires out-of-scope identification. |
| “The system should use AI to help review contracts.” | Actor, actions, outputs, evidence, jurisdiction, and verification method were not defined. | Incomplete / Unverifiable | FR-011 to FR-014, AIR-001 to AIR-003, and UC-003 separate clause identification, extraction, risk detection, source retrieval, and failure behavior. |
| Combined contract-analysis requirement | Clauses, obligations, dates, penalties, risks, and missing information were mixed into one non-atomic statement. | Non-atomic | FR-011, FR-012, and FR-013 separate independently testable outputs. |
| “Fast response” or “reasonable response time.” | No threshold existed for performance acceptance. | Ambiguous / Unverifiable | NFR-001 and NFR-002 define percentile-based response-time targets under the acceptance test load. |
| Generic security requirement | Did not specify credential protection, isolation, file safety, rate limiting, encryption, or secret management. | Incomplete | NFR-004 through NFR-009 and NFR-017 define specific security controls. |
| Private document processing without lifecycle rules | No clear retention, deletion, embedding removal, or training restriction. | Incomplete / Governance gap | FR-026, NFR-011, BR-008, and BR-009 define privacy and deletion behavior. |
| Legal answers without source/version metadata | Users could not verify whether an answer relied on current or applicable authority. | Incomplete / Unverifiable | FR-020, BR-005, AIR-002, AIR-004, AIR-005, and AIR-010 require citation and source metadata. |
| Potential fabricated statutes or citations | A generative model could fill evidence gaps with unsupported legal authority. | AI governance gap | BR-004 and AIR-003 require abstention and prohibit invented legal authority. |
| Conflicting legal sources | Earlier wording did not define behavior when retrieved sources disagree. | Incomplete | BR-006 and AIR-007 require disclosure and citation of competing sources. |
| AI outputs could be treated as final decisions | Human accountability and readiness controls were not explicit enough. | Incomplete / Governance gap | FR-021, BR-007, AIR-012, and UC-007 require human review before binding use. |
| Uploaded document instructions could influence the model | No explicit prompt-injection rule existed in early requirements. | Missing security detail | AIR-008 treats retrieved/uploaded content as untrusted data and requires embedded instructions to be ignored or isolated. |
| Technology choices mixed with requirements | Specific endpoints/vector database details could prematurely constrain the problem specification. | Scope / design contamination | The added requirements remain technology-agnostic; implementation dependencies are separated in Section 9\. |

 

 

## **13\. Requirements Validation** {#13.-requirements-validation}

The corrected requirements were reviewed using the question: “Would the stakeholder interpret this requirement in exactly the same way we do?” The validation criteria below are applied before accepting the specification for design and implementation.

| Criterion | Result | Validation statement | Follow-up |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Correct | Yes | Requirements reflect the documented event-producer workflow, legal/compliance review needs, and the human-in-the-loop objective. | Stakeholder review of scope, use cases, and high-impact legal safeguards remains required. |
| Complete | Conditionally yes | Core functional, quality, business-rule, AI, security, privacy, error/abstention, traceability, and governance needs are represented. | Exact pilot jurisdictions, source corpus, file-size limits, and test-load values must be finalized during implementation planning. |
| Consistent | Yes | No intentional conflict remains between user permissions, source rules, AI behavior, and human approval requirements. | Changes to scope or source governance must be re-reviewed for consistency. |
| Unambiguous | Yes for current baseline | Actors, conditions, outputs, supported scope, and important thresholds are stated explicitly. | Implementation-specific limits should be inserted into configuration and test plans when finalized. |
| Verifiable | Yes | Requirements can be checked using functional tests, security tests, retrieval/citation evaluation, negative tests, workflow-state tests, and audit-log inspection. | Acceptance test cases are linked in the traceability matrix. |
| Feasible | Yes for academic prototype | The capabilities can be implemented incrementally using a web application, curated source base, retrieval, an LLM, secure storage, and explicit human review. | Broad multi-jurisdiction coverage is intentionally excluded from the first release. |
| Traceable | Yes | Requirements are connected to stakeholder/process sources, use cases, project objectives, priorities, and test identifiers. | Traceability should be maintained as requirements change. |
| Prioritized | Yes | Each requirement or requirement group uses MoSCoW priority and core Must decisions are justified. | Any new Must item must be assessed for schedule impact and possible scope change. |

   
Validation result: APPROVED FOR PROJECT DESIGN AND ACADEMIC IMPLEMENTATION, subject to stakeholder confirmation of the pilot jurisdiction/source corpus and completion of implementation-specific test parameters. This is a software-requirements approval, not a legal or regulatory certification.

## **15\. Scope Verification** {#15.-scope-verification}

Each requirement group was compared with the approved scope of a web-based AI Legal Support Assistant for event organization. Items that would substantially expand legal responsibility, platform type, or external-system automation are excluded or deferred.

| Requirement / feature | Scope status | Reason |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Account and role management | In scope | Required to protect case data and administer the system. |
| Event-case creation and context | In scope | Supplies jurisdiction, date, venue, and other facts needed for legal-support workflows. |
| Document upload, extraction, and contract analysis | In scope | Core project workflow documented in the To-Be process. |
| Legal-support chat with citations | In scope | Core project objective, limited to curated event-organization legal content. |
| Event permit/compliance checklist | In scope | Directly supports the identified fragmented manual compliance process. |
| Preliminary contract/clauses | In scope | Allowed only as editable preliminary drafting with disclaimer and human review. |
| Human risk acknowledgement and audit trail | In scope | Required control for high-impact legal-support use. |
| Curated source administration | In scope | Required to maintain source freshness, versioning, and retrieval quality. |
| Responsive web access | In scope | Matches the approved web-application delivery model. |
| Native Android/iOS application | Future version | A mobile app is not required because responsive web access covers the first release. |
| Automated government permit submission | Out of scope | Would require external government integrations and binding filing actions not approved for this release. |
| Autonomous contract signature or payment | Out of scope | Conflicts with the human-review safeguard and would create binding actions. |
| Court representation or litigation strategy | Out of scope | Outside the event-support and preliminary-information project scope. |
| Legal support for jurisdictions without curated sources | Requires approval | Coverage can expand only after authoritative sources, metadata, evaluation, and stakeholder approval are added. |
| Multilingual legal support | Future version | Useful enhancement, but requires additional source validation, language evaluation, and QA. |
| Advanced analytics/dashboard | Future version | Does not determine whether the core legal-support workflow functions. |

   
Any future requirement that significantly changes the approved legal scope, introduces a binding automated action, expands jurisdiction coverage, or adds a major external integration must be submitted as a scope-change proposal rather than silently incorporated.

| :---- | :---- |

| OI-002 | Define implementation-level maximum file size, supported OCR languages, and the document-quality threshold for scanned files. |
| OI-003 | Define the acceptance-test load used for NFR-001 and NFR-002 and document the hardware/hosting environment used during measurement. |

| OI-005 | Confirm retention periods for user documents, audit logs, and deleted-source metadata in accordance with the organization's final privacy policy. |

 

### **Approval / Validation** {#approval-/-validation}

Team validation: The specification is internally consistent with the current A3 As-Is and To-Be processes and with the corrected/audited requirements baseline from the previous planning activity. The requirements are sufficiently explicit to continue into system design, backlog preparation, and test-case development.  
Stakeholder validation required before final baseline: A representative Event Producer and the designated Legal/Compliance Reviewer should confirm the workflow, supported jurisdictions, source corpus, risk-status vocabulary, and human-review checkpoints. Any requested change that expands scope must be processed through the scope-verification rule above.

| Approval role | Validation responsibility | Status |

| Event Producer representative | Validate operational workflow and usability assumptions. | Pending stakeholder review |
| Legal/Compliance Reviewer | Validate legal-support boundaries, source governance, disclaimer, risk review, and human-control safeguards. | Pending stakeholder review |
| Course instructor / project supervisor | Academic approval of SRS deliverable and scope baseline. | Pending review |
